candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record and histopathology clearly show a dual-component lesion: a classic hyperkeratotic seborrheic keratosis with pseudohorn cysts as the background lesion, and an invasive squamous cell carcinoma arising from one lateral end pushing into the dermis with hair involvement, clear cell change (PAS+/diastase sensitive), and high Ki67 (20-40%). The reference diagnosis requires both the SCC component AND its origin in a seborrheic keratosis. C001 captures only the SCC portion without the seborrheic keratosis precursor context or the eyelid site, making it a partial/component match rather than complete equivalence.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Identifies the malignant component (SCC, well-differentiated) but omits the critical composite element: origin/arising within a pre-existing seborrheic keratosis, and lacks the eyelid anatomical specification

case_quality_flags: Composite diagnosis required: malignant transformation of seborrheic keratosis to SCC; single-component candidate misses the precursor lesion
Clear cell change (PAS+/diastase sensitive, Alcian blue/mucicarmine negative) confirms glycogen rather than mucin, supporting SCC over mucoepidermoid or sebaceous carcinoma
Negative adipophilin and androgen receptor effectively excludes sebaceous carcinoma as primary differential
